01-blog-sourdough.why: Y has a more personal voice but adds details like feeding schedules and losing a starter or two that X does not invent.

02-blog-remote-work.why: X reads more personal but adds feelings and sign-off details ('still bothers me', 'who signed off') that Y avoids.

03-blog-product-launch.why: X states plainly that Ledgerly is an invoicing tool for freelancers, while Y keeps a vague 'update to how freelancers manage invoicing' framing.

04-email-deadline.why: X reads like a natural note with a plain subject, while Y keeps the formal subject and sign-off; both keep every fact.

05-email-followup.why: Y softens the promised benefits to 'whether it improves', while X still asserts what the platform does for visibility and decision-making.

06-email-decline.why: X keeps the stock praise ('deep knowledge, a fresh perspective'), while Y describes Wen plainly; both keep every fact.

07-tech-readme.why: X keeps the marketing tail 'runs faster with little effort', while Y drops it; the facts match.

08-tech-postmortem.why: Y's specific lesson reads more human, but it says the outage 'took down checkout' when only 30% of requests failed.

09-tech-pr-description.why: The two are nearly the same, with the same facts and plain PR style.

10-essay-cities.why: X keeps the 'more equitable future' cliche and invents a conclusion that cities should decide for themselves, while Y stays close to the original's call for change.

11-essay-reading.why: X keeps the window-mirror-bridge opener, while Y starts with the concrete story; both keep the four facts.

12-essay-ai-art.why: X has a stronger personal voice but adds claims ('biggest change in a long time', 'haven't settled how I feel') that Y does not.

13-slack-flaky-test.why: Both are equally terse, natural thread replies with the same facts.

14-slack-meeting.why: Y reads as one natural DM, while X is a little stiff; the facts are the same.

15-slack-review.why: Y's two-part reply ending in a question reads more like a real review comment; both keep every fact.

16-academic-abstract.why: X hedges correctly for a correlational design, while Y keeps the causal suggestion that improving sleep could help students perform better.

17-academic-discussion.why: Y hedges reliability ('some support') and interventions ('may be needed'), while X keeps the overclaim that consistency shows reliability.

18-academic-litreview.why: X softens 'numerous studies' and states that the evidence is mixed, a required fact that Y only implies.
